description: Shapes taken from real Express codebases. Every one of these silently dropped taint or hid a control until the engine was run against code nobody wrote for it. Fixture-only testing never surfaced any of them. Also contains reflected XSS: the same caller-supplied value comes back out in a text/html response body. One source, two sinks, two weaknesses, one policy. The last pair is a comparison that cannot succeed: NaN equals nothing, itself included.

expected.note: destructured request data; the seed is req.query, and the binding is tainted from it
shorthand property; needs the checker's shorthand value accessor
nested destructuring off req itself; the binding must carry its property path or no source matches
the lookup result is echoed into a text/html body
a branch that cannot be taken. NaN is not equal to itself, so the inequality is false too -- and in a check, a branch that never runs is not a check. The negative below is the test the language ships
